question: Which statement best describes Main property?
options: `background-color` paints the area behind an element’s content and padding. For example, a pale background can make a help panel easy to distinguish. It is like putting colored paper behind a note. Check that text still has enough contrast, and remember that backgrounds may be disabled in some print settings. For example, give a warning panel a background and a text label so the state is not color-only.

`border` draws a line around an element, with a width, style, and color. For example, `border: 1px solid #bbb` gives a subtle outline. It is like the edge of a card. Use borders to clarify grouping or interaction states, and do not rely on color alone to show that a field has an error. For example, a border can distinguish an input that has keyboard focus.

`background-image` can show a picture, pattern, or gradient behind content. A gradient is a gradual color transition. It is like printing a faint texture on paper. Keep text readable over it, and provide the same meaning in text if the image communicates information. Large decorative images can also increase download time. For example, use a gradient only if text remains readable over every part of it.

`border-radius` rounds the corners of a box. A small radius can soften a card; a fully rounded value can make a pill-shaped button. It is like rounding the corners of a paper ticket. Keep the shape consistent across related controls so users can recognize which elements belong together. For example, a border radius changes shape without changing the content’s meaning.
explanation: `background-color` paints the area behind an element’s content and padding. For example, a pale background can make a help panel easy to distinguish. It is like putting colored paper behind a note. Check that text still has enough contrast, and remember that backgrounds may be disabled in some print settings. For example, give a warning panel a background and a text label so the state is not color-only.
